feedback.finish: Hygiene means keeping yourself and the area around you clean. Good hygiene is important in preventing diseases from spreading.

instruction.text: Match the terms to the correct definitions.

atoms.b: taking care of your body and your surroundings
making sure food is produced and eaten in safe conditions

instruction.text: Select the three images that show good personal hygiene.

feedback.correct1: Bacteria and viruses can live on our clothes if they aren’t washed regularly.
feedback.correct2: Washing our hair and body helps us to keep clean.
feedback.correct3: We pick up most bacteria and viruses on our hands and then touch our mouths or eyes. Washing your hands regularly will prevent the spread of illness.

instruction.text: Drag the cloth to the table to learn more about hygiene.

feedback.finish: Germs live on lots of different surfaces in our surroundings, so cleaning them regularly will reduce the spread of disease.

instruction.text: Read the text about food hygiene and answer the questions.

atoms.text: To maintain good food hygiene, it is important to have clean hands and work equipment. Before coming into contact with food, all knives, pans and chopping boards should be clean.
We also need to make sure that food with an increased risk of bacterial contamination, like chicken, is cooked properly. This means heating things to the correct temperature.
Storing food correctly is another crucial part of having good food hygiene. In order to slow down the spread of germs, most fresh food should be kept in the fridge.

atoms.a: Which of these actions show good food hygiene?
b: turning on every light in the kitchen

atoms.a: How should food be processed properly?
b: ++by heating it to the correct temperature

atoms.a: How should fresh food be stored to prevent illness?

instruction.text: Decide whether these actions are maintaining good food hygiene, personal hygiene or both.
